examples.title: Model A: 65/25/10 sandy loam
examples.situation: A supplied 100 mm example has 65 mm sand, 25 mm silt and 10 mm clay.
reasoning: The three figures sum to 100 mm; the corresponding percentages are 65/25/10.
Under comparable structure and weather, faster drainage and nutrient leaching are plausible concerns.
Carrots, potatoes and rosemary are examples to assess, not an automatic planting list; check moisture supply and the other site requirements.
examples.takeaway: Match the management question to actual conditions.

examples.title: Model B: 40/40/20 loam
examples.situation: A supplied 100 mm example has 40 mm sand, 40 mm silt and 20 mm clay.
reasoning: The point lies in loam on the labelled triangle.
A good structure can provide workable soil with a useful balance of drainage, moisture retention and aeration.
Maize, wheat and many vegetables are examples to consider only after crop and site requirements are checked.
examples.takeaway: Loam is a favourable clue, not a guarantee.

examples.title: Model C: 15/30/55 clay
examples.situation: A supplied 100 mm example has 15 mm sand, 30 mm silt and 55 mm clay.
reasoning: The point lies in the clay class.
Wet workability and poor aeration are possible challenges; cation retention is one possible advantage.
Inspect the actual field's structure and drainage. Choose suitable organic material only after assessing it and the site; use gypsum only if sodicity is diagnosed and reclamation conditions are met.
examples.takeaway: A texture class starts a diagnosis; it does not finish one.
